data.title: bn-3qh0: rebuild-index pack path via offline re-seal request
data.description:
Closes the bn-ccx1 capability regression: rebuild-index was a no-op on pack-sealed segments.

DESIGN: Design B (quarantine plus engine re-seal), not Design A (offline pack encoder). Chosen after two premise-check experiments run before any product code. Premise 1: a rolled segment whose .seal is deleted is NEVER re-sealed by the engine, however many reopens - no candidate means no refutation means no marker means owed_reseal is empty. Premise 2: a bare marker in the segment quarantine slot re-queues the seal, the sealer rebuilds the pack from the log and finalize_footer re-finalizes the footer to name the fresh identity, and the following open admits it with zero refutations.

Design A would duplicate the pack encoder plus the footer-extension encoder outside the engine, keep both in lockstep with PACK_FORMAT_VERSION forever, and rewrite the segment footer - a .log byte, the sole authority - from an offline tool. It also does not escape B: a crash between the pack rename and the footer rewrite is PackIdentityMismatch, which converges only through bn-30u quarantine plus re-seal. No disqualifier for B was found; a withdrawn pack costs the segment its cold tier and nothing else, and every test re-proves byte-exact reads at every step.

KEY FINDING the bone did not anticipate: bn-30u already covers pack ARTIFACTS in full (PRIMARY_EXTENSIONS has seal, quarantine_family knows a pack is self-contained, load_sealed refutes bad packs, check_named_pack refutes mismatches). What it cannot cover is the artifact that is not there. That is the entire regression and the only thing added: an offline withdrawal entry point that can record re-seal intent when there is nothing to rename. It needs NO new marker kind and NO engine code - bn-30u triggers on a structural name parse, never on content, so the request is the segment's own quarantine slot, occupied. engine.rs changes by one doc paragraph.

FLAGS: healthy pack still refused by default (bn-1w4h preserved), --force withdraws it anyway, --reseal opens the store once so the command exits with the pack already rebuilt. A .pidx shadowed by a withdrawn pack is quarantined with it - otherwise an admitted sidecar would silently suppress the very re-seal we requested.

TESTS: mess-store sealed_candidate unit 15/15 (5 new), offline_reseal_request 5/5 new, mess-cli rebuild_pack_path 8/8 new, rebuild_byte_equal 3/3 unchanged-and-passing, full workspace just test 1171 passed 0 failed 28 skipped, cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean, just fmt-check clean, clippy on both crates adds no new warnings.

TERRITORY: no doctor, no inspect, no metrics, no mess-bench. engine.rs is doc-only.
